note: A1+ Unit 3 Lesson 3.6, built on 2026-11-20 under the A1+ lesson standards approved 2026-10-27 and the user's 2026-11-09 rule that every A1+ lesson follows up the A1 lesson with the same number. The user approved the A1+ Unit 3 map on 2026-11-20 (A1+ 3.Y follows A1 3.Y, one step each; A1 Unit 3 has sixteen lessons after the alphabet lessons were removed the same day) and asked for the Unit 2 deal: straight to Preview in batches, Gemini 2.5 Flash photos and ElevenLabs audio pre-approved, no per-lesson gates, reviewed in Preview. Four new photos: twin sisters (both 16), twin brothers (both 18), a brother of 17 and his sister of 19, and two friends who look nothing alike (both 20). They stay out of four-picture cards, where the candles are too small. Nobody in them speaks: the teacher and the co-teacher read every line.

lesson.title: 3.6 Both the same age
lesson.unit_title: Meeting people and talking about them
lesson.unit_outcome: Introduce people and answer introductions, use the short forms of be, answer yes/no questions in short, compare ages, talk about languages, nationalities and jobs, describe people, say whose things are, give an address and say what you want to be.
lesson.goal: Say that two people are twins, are the same age, or are both sixteen (They're both sixteen.).
lesson.grammar_function: A follow-up of A1 3.6 Ages 16-20: A1 asks How old is she? and answers with one age; A1+ 3.6 says what two ages have in common. It adds no new grammar relationship: both goes between they're and the age (They're both sixteen.), the same age follows they're as a description (They're the same age.), and twins is a noun after they're. Two pairs of twins and two other pairs sit behind birthday cakes with number candles from A1 3.6's range, so the ages can be read; twins and the same age are told apart in text, because a picture cannot show who is a twin. 3.4's aren't and 3.5's years older come back (They aren't the same age. She's two years older than him.).
lesson.prerequisite: A1 3.6 sixteen to twenty and How old …?; A1+ 1.5 older; A1+ 3.3 they're; A1+ 3.4 aren't; A1+ 3.5 years older than.
lesson.speaking_outcome: Say both with a long o and a soft th at the end; say the same age as one group. Do not require native-like speed.
